title: Most Pairs Hitting a Target Sum
statement:
You get an array nums and a target k. In one move you remove two entries (at different positions) whose values add up to exactly k. Each entry can be removed only once.

Return the largest number of moves you can make.

examples.why: Remove 2 + 6, 4 + 4 and 5 + 3. The third 4 has no partner left.
Each 5 can be used once, so three 5s make only one pair.
Duplicates make separate pairs: two 1s with two 7s. Counting distinct value pairs would give 1.

hints: Does it matter which 4 you pair with which 4, or which partner a value gets, as long as the sum is k?
Each value v can only pair with k − v. So pairing is never a hard choice: just match as many as possible.
Sort and use two pointers from both ends: equal to k means a pair, too small moves the left pointer, too big moves the right one. Or count values in a hash map as you go.

explain.intuition:
A value v can only pair with the value k − v. There is no competition between different values, so greed is safe: any time two remaining entries sum to k, removing them never blocks a better plan.

After sorting, two pointers find the pairs. If nums[lo] + nums[hi] is too small, the smallest value cannot pair with anything left (its best partner, the largest, is not enough), so drop it. If it is too big, the largest cannot pair with anything, so drop it. If it equals k, count a pair and drop both. Alternatively, a hash map of unmatched values does it in one pass: for each value, use a waiting k − v if there is one, else add v to the waiting list.
steps: If s === k: count a pair, move both pointers inward.
If s < k: move lo right. Otherwise move hi left.
pitfalls: Pairing an entry with itself when v = k − v. A single 4 is not a pair for k = 8.
Counting distinct value combinations instead of entries. [1, 1, 7, 7] has two pairs.
Counting all occurrences of v and k − v at the end and adding min for both v and k − v, which counts every pair twice.

complexity.time: O(n log n) with sorting, O(n) with a hash map
complexity.space: O(1) extra after sorting, or O(n) for the map

solutions.title: Pair the first match for each entry
solutions.idea: For each unused entry, scan for any unused partner that completes k and remove both.

solutions.title: Sort and two pointers
solutions.idea: After sorting, the smallest and largest remaining values decide which one can be dropped.

solutions.title: Hash map of waiting values
solutions.idea: Keep counts of values still waiting for a partner. Each new value either completes a waiting k − v or starts waiting itself.

followups: Each move now removes three entries summing to k. Is greedy still safe?
Return the pairs themselves, in the order they were found.
